text.en: Raju noticed that table salt dissolves in water but sugar does not conduct electricity. "Their bonds must be different," he said.

Atoms combine to form molecules and the attractive force that holds them is a chemical bond. Kossel and Lewis explained this in 1916 by the octet rule: atoms combine to gain the stable electronic configuration of a noble gas, usually eight electrons in the outer shell.
In an ionic or electrovalent bond one atom gives electrons and another takes them, forming positive and negative ions held by electrostatic attraction. The number of electrons lost or gained is the electrovalency. In magnesium chloride, magnesium has 2, 8, 2 and loses two electrons while each chlorine with 2, 8, 7 gains one.
In a covalent bond atoms share electrons. Lewis dot structures show the outer electrons as dots. The kind of bond decides the properties of the compound. Oxidation is loss of electrons and reduction is gain of electrons.

problem.en: Sodium (2, 8, 1) and chlorine (2, 8, 7) combine. What happens?

text.en: Sodium loses its one outer electron.
Na+ and Cl- attract to form the ionic bond in NaCl.

prompt.en: A friend says In an ionic bond electrons are shared equally. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Ionic bonds involve transfer of electrons.

points.en: Atoms bond to get a noble gas arrangement.
Ionic bond: transfer; covalent bond: sharing.
Oxidation is loss, reduction is gain of electrons.
